cards.explanation: The answer is fire. The text says fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp. That came after He heard their complaining and His anger was kindled. Imagine pulling a tray and the edges are the first thing to go. That's the outskirts, friends.

The answer is Moses. The text says the people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down. They came to the one who was leading them, and he took it straight to the LORD. That's a good habit for any of us when things start burning.

The answer is that the fire of the LORD burned there. The text says the place was called Taberah, “…because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.” So the name itself carried the reminder of what happened there. The Millers carved "Dorin" into my handle, and honestly, a name sticks around a long time.

The answer is meat. They say, “Who will feed us meat?” The text says the rabble among them had a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites wept. They had manna in front of them, but they were asking for meat. Even I get itchy for a different cookie sometimes.

The answer is Egypt. They remember the fish they ate freely there, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic. The word that jumps out at me is "freely." Their memory of that menu is doing a lot of work for them.

The answer is True. The people say, “But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing to see but this manna!” That's their complaint in their own words. They had just been listing the foods they remembered from Egypt, and then they point at the manna.

The answer is pastry baked with fine oil. The text says the manna “…tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.” Everybody in that camp had a bakery's worth of flavor falling from the sky, and they were still complaining. I'd have hired a taster for that.
The answer is True. The text says when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell with it. So it showed up with the dew, right at the camp. Nobody had to preheat anything.

The answer is displeased. The text says Moses heard the people of family after family weeping at the entrances to their tents, and “…Moses was also displeased.” The anger of the LORD was kindled greatly at the same time. I think that's a lot to take in from every tent.

The answer is a nurse carrying an infant. Moses asks the LORD whether he conceived all these people or gave them birth. Then he says the LORD told him, “Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant…” That's a lot of baby for one man to hold.

The answer is False. Moses says, “I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.” He tells the LORD plainly it's too much. Notice he brings it to the LORD instead of keeping it in.

The answer is that Moses asks the LORD to kill him right now. He says, “…please kill me right now…” I think this one hurts, friends. He says it right after telling the LORD the burden of all these people is too much for him.

The answer is that they help Moses bear the burden of the people. The LORD says, “They will help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself.” Moses had just said he couldn't carry them alone. And here's the LORD answering that very thing.

The answer is month. The LORD says they'll eat it “…but for a whole month…” He counts the days up first: one or two, then five or ten or twenty. Then He says month. That's a long stretch with one menu.

The reason the text gives is that they rejected the LORD who is among them. The LORD says, “…because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you…” They also cried out, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?” It's about turning away from the LORD, not just about food.

The answer is True. Moses asks, “If all our flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? Or if all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?” He's doing the math out loud. And it doesn't add up for him.

The answer is that they prophesy. The text says the LORD came down in the cloud and took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. Then comes the line: “As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied…” Seventy elders at once, friends. That's a full tray.

The answer is False, friends. The Spirit rested on the seventy elders and they prophesied, but the text says they never did so again (Numbers 11:25). It happened that one time. Like a cookie box that gets one star and then the sky just keeps shining on its own, that day was a one-time moment and the text doesn't say more.

The answer is that the Spirit rests on them and they prophesy. Eldad and Medad were among those listed but had not gone out to the tent, and “…the Spirit rested on them…” They prophesied right there in the camp. Not being at the tent didn't stop it.
The answer is stop them. Joshua is Moses' attendant, and he speaks up: “Moses, my lord, stop them!” Eldad and Medad were prophesying in the camp. Joshua wanted it shut down.

The answer is prophets. Moses first asks Joshua, “Are you jealous on my account?” Then he says, “I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!” That's his answer after Joshua says, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”

The answer is a day's journey in every direction. The quail are brought near the camp “…for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.” That's a lot of ground to cover in birds. I'd hate to be the one holding the broom.
The answer is False. The text says, “All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail.” That's a day, a night and the next day. Not exactly a one-morning job.
The answer is a severe plague. The text says, “…the LORD struck them with a severe plague.” It happened while the meat was still between their teeth. This part is heavy, friends.

The answer is craved. The text says they called the place Kibroth-hattaavah, “…because there they buried the people who had craved other food.” The name records that people were buried there. I think this one is heavy, friends, and the name keeps the craving in front of us.
